description: Sets up or changes one video type of one of the business's video series, with every choice the Series page's video type editor has, saved the way that page saves it (its same checks; everything else in the series kept as it is). Give series and type to change that type: only the choices given change. Leave type out to add a new type; give newSeries instead of series to make a new draft video series for it. remove: true takes a type off. Full creative freedom: looks drawn (motion graphics in code), clips (AI video), stills or mix; any length from 5 seconds; the shape in the owner's words; narrated, the characters talking, or no voice at all; music and its style; words on screen; research; how many a week; asking first; quality. For example a seamless 12-second loop with no voice: shape 'a seamless 12-second loop of one satisfying moment', length {min: 12, max: 12}, heard none, music true. What it costs: how a type is made sets what each episode may use; an episode in AI video is priced as a film with AI video on the owner's plan, much more than one in motion graphics (a higher quality and more a week cost more too). The answer gives each type's tokens an episode and a month as the change leaves it, and the month before: tell the owner what it now costs. On a running series a change that raises what its month may use is refused unless monthlyTokens is the new month the owner agreed to in their own words; an episode dearer than the budget kept at Start no longer goes ahead on that budget: it follows the business's Series episodes choice (a card asking the owner first, unless that choice already lets it go ahead). A draft spends nothing until the owner starts it (series_start, or Start on its page). Changing a type is free. It needs an act key.

askFirst.description: each one the calendar makes waits for the owner's yes on its script first

captions.description: words on screen: spoken (the spoken words, as they are said), titles (short title cards only) or none. With nobody heard, the words are titles

body.description: the face for captions and running text

display.description: the face for titles and cards

fonts.description: the faces its films are set in, by role (a family Marsell has, or one of the business's own fonts); null: the series' own

heard.description: who is heard: narrator (one voice reads it), characters (the speakers talk in their own voices) or none (no voice at all: any words are read on screen as titles)

length.description: its length in seconds, any range from 5 up: {min: 12, max: 12} for a 12-second loop, {min: 30, max: 60} for a Short, {min: 480, max: 720} for a film of 8 to 12 minutes

looks.description: how it is made: drawn (motion graphics made in code: animated type, shapes and the business's own pictures, no generated video), clips (AI video: every shot a generated video clip), stills (pictures moved in the edit) or mix (about half generated clips, half pictures). An episode in AI video costs much more than one in motion graphics

master4k.description: a 4K copy beside each film, for ads

monthlyTokens.description: on a running series, the month's tokens the owner agreed to for the series as this change leaves it (the refusal says the number)

musicStyle.description: the music, in words: 'warm lo-fi piano, slow'

name.description: the video type's name, as the owner calls it

narrator.description: with heard narrator: the character who narrates, by id (series_video_types_read characters), or null for a voice-over. A series whose cast has a narrator is narrated by them in every narrated type; left out, that narrator

narratorStyle.description: Mr Narrator Guy, the studio's own narrator style: his voice and his delivery; null: none

narratorVoice.description: the voice the series' narrator speaks in, in every type it narrates: only a voice the project kept (series_video_types_read voices.kept, or voices_read). A stock voice goes in voiceOver instead, with heard narrator; a type nobody narrates needs neither

newSeries.description: instead of series: makes a new video series for this type, as a draft (its name, and what it is about and who it is for in the owner's words). Nothing is made, spent or posted until the owner starts it

about.description: what it is about and who it is for, in the owner's words

perWeek.description: how many the calendar makes a week, 0 to 21 (7 is every day, 14 twice a day); 0: only when the owner asks

pictures.description: made (pictures may be made) or real (only the business's own pictures and real archives: stills or drawn only, since clips are made by a video model)

project.description: The project's id or exact name. Optional when the account has one project.

quality.description: the picture quality: standard (768p), hd (1080p) or 2k; null: the plan's own (Standard on Solo, else HD). Higher costs more

references.description: films the owner liked for this type, each with a link and what they liked about it, which the director reads (path null); the whole list, replacing the one it had

path.description: one of the series' own files by its storage path; null from here

words.description: what the owner liked about it, in their words

remove.description: true takes the type off the series

research.description: a research pass with sources before each script

series.description: the video series, by its id or exact name (series_video_types_read)

shape.description: what happens in it, in the owner's words: 'a seamless 12-second loop of one satisfying moment', 'one news story: what was found, where, and why it matters'

speakers.description: with heard characters: the characters heard in their own voices, by id

timezone.description: the owner's time zone, IANA ('Europe/Berlin'), for a type newly on the schedule; left out, the series' own, else UTC

type.description: the video type to change, by its id or exact name. Leave out to add a new type (with newSeries: the new series' first type, its Short, is set up)

voiceOver.description: with heard narrator and no narrating character: the voice-over's voice, a kept voice's voiceId or a stock voice's id (series_video_types_read voices); null: Marsell's default narrator

voiceOverModel.description: the model the voice-over speaks in: Eleven v4 (takes directions) or Multilingual v2 (read straight)

name: series_video_type_set
title: Series video type set
